summary: Takatsugu Hayashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Delhi. He taught Yōhei Furukawa and held positions at Tohoku University (until 1997), National Institute of Technology, Sendai College, and Hosen Gakuen College.

Takayasu Kimura (1934–2017) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (~1957–1963). He held academic posts as a researcher at the Buzan-ha Institute of Modern Mission and as a lecturer at Taisho University.

Takayasu Suzuki (born 1964) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1983 to 1994 and served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University around 2004.

Takayoshi Namikawa (born 1947) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Bukkyo University (~1966–1977). He taught Satoshi Hiraoka and served as a professor at Bukkyo University from circa 1994 to 2002.

Takayuki Hirosawa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen (~1978–1981), was a group member at Taisho University until 1991, and served as professor at Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Takechika Fukado is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He pursued his doctoral studies at Bukkyo University under the supervision of Seitetsu Moriyama, completing his degree by 2010.

Takeo Hibino (1914–2007) was a sinology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1935–1938). He held academic posts at Otemon Gakuin University (~1978–1983) and Otemae University (~1983–1993).

Takeshi Fujii (born 1955) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1974–1980), where he later held a post from circa 1992 to 2021 and taught Kei Kataoka.

Takeshi Umehara (1925–2019) was a philosophy and Japanology scholar educated at Kyoto and Nagoya Universities. He held posts at Ryukoku, Ritsumeikan (~1952–1972), the International Research Center for Japanese Studies as director general (~1987–1995), and the Institute of Technologists (~2001–2011).
Takumi Fukuda (born 1963) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hajime Sakurabe. From 1995 to 2002, he served as a full-time lecturer at Doho University.

Takudo Ishikawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as a researcher at the Jodo Shu Research Institute until 2005 and held a post as a specially appointed full-time lecturer at Taisho University.

Takushu Sugimoto (born 1935), a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology, earned his PhD at Tohoku University (-1981). He held professorships at Kanazawa University (~1974–2000), Komazawa University (~2000–2006), and Kinjo University (~2006).

Tan Chung (1929–2024) was a scholar of sinology, history, and Indology. He taught Yukteshwar Kumar and Sabaree Mitra, served as Professor of Chinese at Delhi University (~1964–1978), and headed Chinese and Japanese Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1978–1994).

Tansen Sen specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Peking University (~1988–1991) and earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania (~1991–2000) under Victor H. Mair, later serving at Baruch College (~2002–2017).

Tanya Zivkovic is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who studied under the traditional teacher Dawa. She held a position as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the University of Adelaide from circa 2009 to 2014.

Tao Jiang is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from Temple University (~1996–2001) under Shigenori Nagatomo. Around 2009, he served as Associate Professor in the Department of Religion at Rutgers University.

Tao Jin is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2002–2008) under the doctoral supervision of Alexander L. Mayer, with Brian D. Ruppert serving as a committee member.

Tao Pan is a scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He earned a BA from Fudan University (~2006–2010) and subsequently completed a Magister Artium at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2010–2014).

Tarab Tulku (1934–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. From circa 1962 to 1998, he held academic positions at the University of Copenhagen and served as a curator at the Royal Danish Library.

Tarif Khalidi (born 1938) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at University College, Oxford (~1957–1960) and the University of Chicago (~1966–1970), later holding posts at the American University of Beirut (~1970) and Cambridge (~1996–2002).
